title: I Let Payroll Keep Volunteer Saturday as Unpaid Until HR Read It

parts.text: I got the calendar invite at 3:12 p.m.: VOLUNTEER SATURDAY — MANDATORY SMILES. I was twenty-nine, warehouse admin, already at forty hours. I replied-all asking if it was paid. My manager, Tam, wrote: volunteer means volunteer. I screenshotted the word mandatory. I went anyway in a company shirt they made me buy. I scanned boxes for six hours. The badge reader logged it. Monday payroll showed zero. I forwarded the invite, the badge log, and the shirt receipt to HR with subject: mandatory volunteer. Tam called me ungrateful on the floor. Then she posted a photo of us "giving back" on LinkedIn tagged with the company page.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She posted the unpaid Saturday on LinkedIn with the company tag.

social.video_title: Mandatory volunteer Saturday hit payroll as zero — Part 1/2
social.description: Forty hours already, a company shirt I paid for, and a badge log that still counts. Then LinkedIn. Would you have skipped it?

parts.text: HR asked Tam if attendance was optional. The invite said mandatory. The photo had twenty-two employees. They paid the Saturday as overtime and banned mandatory volunteer language. I got the hours on the next check and a reimbursement for the shirt. Tam deleted the LinkedIn post. I still volunteer when it is actually volunteer, which is never on a badge reader. The calendar is quieter. My smiles are unpaid only when I offer them. The boxes got scanned either way, but now the scan has a rate.

social.video_title: HR paid the Saturday after the LinkedIn photo — Part 2/2
social.description: Badge logs, a shirt receipt, and a word that cannot be both mandatory and free. Was a smile ever a wage?
